newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Volvo's Swedish car sales down 10 pct '96.
newsitem.headline: Volvo's Swedish car sales down 10 pct '96.

text.p: Swedish automotive group AB Volvo said on Thursday that its Swedish car sales dropped more than 10 percent in 1996 to 43,681 cars from 48,982 cars the previous year.

"The company car discussions going on in 1996 have affected sales of our large cars, but now the legislation is known by everybody," Bent Nissen, head of media relations at Volvo Cars Sweden, told Reuters.
Nissen was referring to new company car tax legislation that took effect in Sweden on January 1, 1997, which quelled fears that rules would change drastically.
"Our aim is to hold around 25 percent of the Swedish market in the future," he said.
Volvo 800 (S70/V70) fell to 22,664 registrations last year, from 24,514 the previous year, while Volvo 900 (S/V90) decreased to 13,290 registrations from 19,351.
But Volvo S40/V40 rose to 6,752 registrations in 1996 from 27 a year earlier.
And 1997 looks brighter for Volvo Cars in Sweden, according to Nissen.
"It looks positive for the start of 1997," Nissen said. "Interest for the 850-series follow-up, the S70/V70, is large and order bookings are already higher than expected."
Volvo expects to be able to deliver the first cars of the new model to customers at the end of January or beginning of February, Nissen said.
